originalTitle: The Peer-Group Mispricing Sitting On LOW Stock
summary: In the home improvement aisle, one giant's performance metrics are climbing while its stock price lags the broader market, asking investors to decide if it's a bargain or a trap.
content:
In the home improvement aisle, one giant’s performance metrics are climbing while its stock price lags the broader market, asking investors to decide if it’s a bargain or a trap.

Lowe’s Companies (LOW) stock is trading around $221.25 a share, having delivered a return of -6.4% over a twelve-month period where the S&P 500 gained 22%. But inside its own competitive group, a stark mismatch appears. Lowe’s delivers results near the top of its class on growth and profitability, yet its stock carries one of the group’s cheaper price tags. The question for investors is simple: has the market correctly sniffed out trouble ahead, or is this a case of strong performance going unrewarded?

Image by Steve Buissinne from Pixabay

Lowe’s Outperforms Where It Counts.

When lined up against its direct competitors , Lowe’s operational results stand out. The company grew revenue by 6.2% over the last twelve months, a figure that puts it at the top of its peer group and well ahead of the 2.2% growth posted by its larger rival, Home Depot. Its operating margin of 11.5% is also solid, ranking third in the group and comfortably beating names like Floor & Decor, which posted a margin of 6.1%.

Despite this strong delivery, the market assigns Lowe’s a valuation near the bottom of the pack. The stock trades at 18.6 times earnings. That’s a steep discount to Home Depot at 25.1 times and specialty retailer Sherwin-Williams at 33.1 times. In fact, Lowe’s valuation is more in line with Tractor Supply, which trades at 18.3 times earnings but is a much smaller company with lower growth.

The market’s hesitation is rooted in the American homeowner. Management is clear that “DIY demand remains under pressure” amid a “challenging housing environment.” This is the core of the bear case: Lowe’s growth is coming from a narrow, and potentially fragile, base. While the company’s focus on professional contractors is paying off, the foundation of its business is still the do-it-yourself customer, who is pulling back on big projects.

This tension shows up in the details. In the last quarter, comparable transactions declined 0.9%, meaning fewer customers came through the doors. The company still posted positive comparable sales because the average ticket increased 1.5%, driven by Pros and essential repairs. The market is effectively pricing in the risk that this trend is unsustainable. With about one-third of Lowe’s business tied to discretionary categories, a continued slowdown from the DIY segment could easily overwhelm the gains from the Pro business. This concern is underscored by management’s own forecast that adjusted diluted earnings per share in the second quarter will be “approximately 2% below prior year.”

The Metric That Will Settle the Score.

While the market’s caution is understandable, Lowe’s is actively working to counter the macro pressures through its “Total Home strategy.” The company is driving growth in areas less exposed to DIY whims, evidenced by a 15.5% increase in online sales last quarter and a push into services. It is also rolling out new tools like AI-Driven Material Lists to deepen its relationship with professional customers. For investors looking for a way to participate in this sector, a consumer discretionary ETF like XLY offers broad exposure.

The entire debate boils down to whether these internal initiatives can generate enough momentum to offset the sluggish housing market. The clearest test of this will be the company’s own full-year target. Management has affirmed its outlook for “comparable sales in a range of flat to up 2%.” Hitting the upper end of that range would be a strong signal that the strategy is working. Falling short of the low end, or cutting the outlook altogether, would suggest the market’s caution was warranted.

chineseTitle: 同行集团因库存不足而定价错误
chineseSummary: 在家居装修领域，一家巨头的业绩指标正在攀升，而其股价却落后于大盘，这要求投资者判断这是便宜货还是陷阱。
chineseContent:
在家居装修领域，一家巨头的业绩指标正在攀升，而其股价却落后于大盘，这要求投资者判断这是便宜货还是陷阱。

Lowe’s Companies (LOW) 股票交易价格约为每股 221.25 美元，在过去 12 个月内回报率为 -6.4%，而标准普尔 500 指数上涨了 22%。但在其自己的竞争群体内部，却出现了明显的不匹配。劳氏 (Lowe's) 在增长和盈利能力方面的业绩在同类公司中名列前茅，但其股票的价格却是该集团中较便宜的之一。投资者面临的问题很简单：市场是否正确地嗅出了未来的麻烦，或者这是强劲表现却得不到回报的情况？

该图片由Steve Buissinne在Pixabay上发布

劳氏 (Lowe’s) 的表现优于其他公司。

与直接竞争对手相比，劳氏的运营业绩脱颖而出。该公司在过去 12 个月的收入增长了 6.2%，这一数字使其在同行中名列前茅，远远领先于其规模更大的竞争对手家得宝 (Home Depot) 2.2% 的增长。其 11.5% 的营业利润率也很稳健，在集团中排名第三，轻松击败了 Floor & Decor 等公司，后者的利润率为 6.1%。

尽管交货强劲，但市场对劳氏的估值接近垫底。该股的市盈率为 18.6 倍。这比家得宝 (Home Depot) 的 25.1 倍和专业零售商宣伟 (Sherwin-Williams) 的 33.1 倍都有大幅折扣。事实上，Lowe’s 的估值与 Tractor Supply 更为一致，后者的市盈率为 18.3 倍，但规模要小得多，增长率也较低。

市场的犹豫根源在于美国房主。管理层明确表示，在“充满挑战的住房环境”中，“DIY 需求仍然面临压力”。这是悲观观点的核心：劳氏的增长来自狭窄且可能脆弱的基础。尽管该公司对专业承包商的关注正在取得回报，但其业务的基础仍然是DIY客户，他们正在撤回大型项目。

这种张力体现在细节上。上个季度，可比交易量下降了 0.9%，这意味着进店的顾客减少了。该公司的可比销售额仍然为正，因为在专业人士和必要维修的推动下，平均票价增长了 1.5%。市场实际上已经消化了这种趋势不可持续的风险。 Lowe’s 约三分之一的业务与非必需品类相关，DIY 领域的持续放缓很容易压倒专业业务的收益。管理层自己的预测强调了这种担忧，即第二季度调整后的稀释每股收益将“比去年同期低约 2%”。

决定胜负的指标。

虽然市场的谨慎态度是可以理解的，但 Lowe's 正在通过其“整体家居策略”积极应对宏观压力。该公司正在推动较少受 DIY 奇思妙想影响的领域的增长，上季度在线销售额增长 15.5% 以及进军服务领域就证明了这一点。它还推出了人工智能驱动的材料列表等新工具，以加深与专业客户的关系。对于寻求参与该行业的投资者来说，像 XLY 这样的非必需消费品 ETF 可以提供广泛的投资机会。

整个争论归结为这些内部举措是否能够产生足够的动力来抵消低迷的房地产市场。最明显的考验将是公司自己的全年目标。管理层确认了“可比销售额增长 2% 至持平”的前景。触及该范围的上限将是一个强烈信号，表明该策略正在发挥作用。低于低端，或完全下调前景，表明市场的谨慎是有道理的。

这件作品拉动了一根线；我们完整的 LOW 点对点仪表板并排放置了每个指标，并且每天更新。

排名变化。纪律化合物。

每个财报季，同行排行榜都会重新洗牌：领先者下滑，落后者迎头赶上，溢价出现又消失。逐名追洗牌是一份全职工作，命中率不高。

Trefis High Quality (HQ) 投资组合跳过了追逐：大约 30 家优质企业拥有持久的基本面，根据规则而不是排名表进行规模和重新平衡。它有着超越三大主要指数（标准普尔 500 指数、标准普尔中型股指数和罗素 2000 指数）的基准的记录。把你的钱锚定在纪律上。
